blurb:
She came in underweight from animal control, and now she's in a Prison Pups training program learning skills and soaking up structure. Monica is about a year old, 35 pounds, a hound mix with a whole lot of heart and a separation anxiety problem that she's working hard to get past.

Her energy level sits around a 4 to 6 and the volunteers describe her as sweet, gentle, and genuinely devoted to the people she loves. She's happy when she's with you. The hard part is when she's not. She needs a home where someone is around most of the time — remote work, work-from-home, stay-at-home, doesn't matter — she just needs to know her person isn't gone forever. A Mostly Mutts trainer will help you work through that with her.

She's done well meeting other dogs and would probably thrive with a calm, good-natured dog at home. She met a couple of young boys and got a little jumpy when they ran, so kids 15 and up are a better fit. She's also heartworm positive right now, which means she'll need local adoption and will have some activity restrictions during treatment — but that's being handled.

Call 770-272-6888 to find out when Monica is available to meet. She's off-site for training, so you'll need to check in first before heading over.
scoring_notes:
• Prison Pups program participation is a compelling, human-interest story readers will remember
• Multiple adoption considerations — heartworm treatment, separation anxiety, kids 15+ — narrow the pool but deepen the story
• Off-site training and medical treatment signal she has been in the system long enough to require structured intervention

blurb:
A volunteer was sitting outside on a rock with Adina and she just crawled right into their lap. That pretty much tells you what you need to know about this dog.

She's five years old, about 42 pounds, a terrier mix who went through the Mostly Mutts Prison Pups training program and came out the other side friendly, active, and genuinely sweet. Her foster put it plainly: "this girl is so sweet, smart, and friendly. I'm not sure which she enjoys more — her walks or naps." She's done day trips with a volunteer, walked in the woods, sniffed everything, even dipped her toes in a creek. She's game for adventure and also perfectly happy to come home and crash afterward.

She can be a little shy when she first meets new people, and she might bark at people or dogs on walks while she's still building her confidence. She's making progress on that every day with her trainer. She did well with kids around six years old at the rescue, so kids ten and up should be a solid fit. She's also open to meeting other dogs if you've got one at home.

Adina is at Mostly Mutts in Kennesaw. Call 770-272-6888 or visit mostlymutts.org to start the process.
scoring_notes:
• Lap-crawl volunteer moment is an instantly shareable, visually rich anecdote that anchors the whole blurb
• Prison Pups graduate narrative combined with creek hikes and couch naps gives her the widest lifestyle appeal of the dog candidates
• Five years old with ongoing confidence-building training suggests a meaningful shelter tenure and real urgency to place her

blurb:
Ten years old, nine pounds, and she has been through it. Rae came to Mostly Mutts from a neglectful situation, went through animal control first, and needed a good stretch of time and care before she was ready to find a home. That time has passed. She's had her spay, a dental, and a mammary mass removal. She is ready.

She's not a dog who's going to demand your attention. Her foster describes her days as napping, a little exploring, collecting some petting, and then more napping. She's curious but calm. Gentle and quiet. She does have some hearing loss, so she responds better to louder sounds, a whistle, or a tap on the leg than to standard voice commands — her foster has that routine down and it works fine. Mostly Mutts also offers free lifetime training classes with adoption, so you'd have support figuring out what works best.

She lives with other dogs in her foster home and basically ignores them, which is perfect if you have a dog who isn't looking for a new best friend. Older kids who know to be careful around a small senior dog would be a good fit too.

Rae is in foster care right now. Reach out to Mostly Mutts at 770-272-6888 to set up a time to meet her.
scoring_notes:
• Neglect-to-recovery arc with spay, dental, and tumor removal signals a long, meaningful journey — maximum emotional pull
• Senior, hearing-impaired, 9-pound dog is a statistically hard adoption, making her feature-worthy on urgency alone
• 'She is ready' framing after an extended recovery period is a direct call to action that translates perfectly to print

blurb:
Big paws at two months old is basically a promise. Benny is a tabby boy, one of nine kittens born after Mostly Mutts rescued his mama while she was still pregnant. The whole litter has been growing up in foster homes ever since, and Benny has spent that time doing what he does best: wrestling his siblings and then flopping over on his people when he's tired.

His foster describes him as friendly, playful, and always up for a good wrestling match. But when playtime winds down, he switches gears fast. He's a snuggler. The kind of kitten who will absolutely wear you out chasing a toy around the room and then immediately want to sit on you. If you've been on the fence about getting a cat, spending ten minutes with Benny will probably make the decision for you.

He gets along great with his littermates, so another cat at home is a plus. His history with dogs isn't known yet, and kids are welcome as long as they're gentle with something this small. He's litter trained, microchipped, and has started his vaccines. You'll finish the kitten series as he grows. Neuter is required and Mostly Mutts covers that cost through an approved North Metro vet once he's ready.

Go to mostlymutts.org to submit an adoption inquiry and set up a visit.

blurb:
He's the smallest of nine siblings, and somehow he's also the cuddliest. Puck is a two-month-old tabby boy who came into the world when Mostly Mutts rescued his pregnant mama and let the whole litter be born safe and warm in foster care. All nine of them. Puck is the little one who figured out the best seat in the house isn't on the couch. It's on your shoulder.

He'll do a full lap of zoomies around the room, burn through every bit of kitten energy he has, and then immediately find the nearest warm lap and park himself there. That's his whole routine. Run hard, cuddle harder. If you're working from home and need a tiny coworker who insists on sitting at shoulder height, this is your guy.

Puck gets along great with his siblings, so another cat in the house would probably make him very happy. His history with dogs is unknown, but he's been raised in a busy foster home and handles activity well. He's litter trained, microchipped, and has started his kitten vaccines. You'll finish those as he grows. Spay/neuter is required and Mostly Mutts covers that cost through one of their approved North Metro vets.

Head to mostlymutts.org to submit an inquiry and set up a time to meet him.

blurb:
At some point during a visit outside, Adina climbed into someone's lap while they were sitting on a rock. Not a couch. A rock. That's the kind of dog she is.

She's five years old, about 42 pounds, and went through the Mostly Mutts Prison Pups training program, so she's had real, structured instruction. Her foster summed her up pretty well: "I'm not sure which she enjoys more, her walks or her naps." She's done day trips out in the woods, gone wading in the water on hot days, and handles car rides without drama. She gets baths like a champ and the volunteers say her coat is genuinely beautiful.

She can be a little shy with new people at first, and she may bark on walks when she spots other dogs or strangers coming. That's not aggression, just her working through confidence stuff that she's actively getting better at every day with her trainer. Give her a little time to warm up and she settles right in. She got along well with other dogs in the training program and met some young kids at the shelter without issue, though a home with kids ten and up is probably the smoothest fit.

Adina is a really solid, well-rounded dog who just needs the right family to give her room to be herself. Stop by Mostly Mutts in Kennesaw or call 770-272-6888 to set up a meeting.

blurb:
She came in from animal control a little underweight and a little unsure, but Monica has been putting in the work. This one-year-old hound mix is currently in Mostly Mutts' Prison Pups training program, which means she's spending her days learning manners and building confidence in a real structured environment. By the time she's ready to come home with you, she's going to be way ahead of most dogs her age.

She's friendly, sweet, and genuinely just wants to be near her people. That's the whole thing with Monica. She's happiest when someone is around, and she struggles when she's left alone for long stretches. So she's not the right fit for someone who's gone ten hours a day, but if you work from home or have a flexible schedule, she's going to be an easy dog to love. A Mostly Mutts trainer will help you work through any separation anxiety once she's settled in.

A heads up: Monica is heartworm positive and will be going through treatment, so local adoption only for now, and her activity level needs to stay a bit lower until she's cleared. She's done great with other calm, friendly dogs and would probably do well with another easygoing pup in the house. Kids 15 and up are a good match.

Call 770-272-6888 to find out when Monica is available to meet. She's worth the wait.
scoring_notes:
• Prison Pups training program is a proven human-interest angle that elevates her above a standard shelter dog narrative
• Heartworm treatment and separation anxiety create real adoption friction, but also real urgency — she needs the right reader to step up

blurb:
Ten years old, nine pounds, and she has already been through more than most dogs twice her size. Rae came to Mostly Mutts out of a neglectful situation, spent some time at animal control getting the care she needed, and has now made it through a spay, a dental, and a mammary mass removal. She's on the other side of all of it. And according to the people who know her best, she's doing great.

Her daily routine right now is basically a masterclass in taking it easy: nap, short walk, collect some petting, nap again. She's curious and likes to explore at her own pace, but she's not going to demand a lot from you. She lives with other dogs in her foster home and gets along fine with them, mostly by ignoring them entirely, which honestly sounds like the ideal roommate situation. She's friendly and sweet, just not a lap dog. She'll appreciate your attention without being needy about it.

One thing worth knowing: Rae is hard of hearing. She responds better to louder sounds or a whistle than to voice commands, and her foster has found that a leg tap works well to get her attention. Mostly Mutts offers free lifetime training classes with every adoption, and they've got good ideas for working with hearing-impaired dogs.

She'd do best with older or gentler kids, and cats are unknown. If you're looking for a quiet, low-key companion who's already been through the hard stuff, Rae is ready for a soft landing. Reach out to Mostly Mutts at 770-272-6888 to meet her.
scoring_notes:
• Survived neglect, animal control, a spay, a dental, and a mass removal — her resilience story is the most emotionally powerful in this batch
• Senior, hearing-impaired, and nine pounds: the underdog profile that reliably moves newsletter readers to act and share
• Longest and hardest road to readiness signals extended shelter time — high urgency for a soft landing before reader fatigue sets in
